title: Truth cannot be forced on a closed heart.
subtitle: Nuh refuses to push what they hate

row.title: his people
sub: they did not see its worth

then: Nuh's people had just called him an ordinary man followed by the lowest of them. He answered calmly. He had {idea}clear proof and a mercy from his Lord{/idea}, but it was hidden from their eyes, so they rushed to reject it. {trap}Should we force it on you while you hate it?{/trap}
now: Your brother scoffs every time you mention prayer at the family dinner. You feel the urge to win, to corner him with arguments until he gives in. {idea}Nuh did not force.{/idea} He kept the door open and his voice gentle.
old: If I care about someone, I should push until they agree.
new: My job is to make the truth clear; opening the heart is not mine to force.
try: Next time faith comes up with someone who resists, say one kind sentence and then let it rest.

title: He asked for no money and dropped no one.
subtitle: Nuh refuses to send the poor believers away

row.title: the chiefs
sub: too important to sit with them

then: The chiefs wanted Nuh to separate himself from the believers, because they felt {trap}too important to sit with them{/trap}. Quraysh later asked the Prophet ﷺ the same thing, to hold a private gathering just for the elite. Nuh said he took {reward}no payment, his reward was with Allah{/reward}, and he would not drive anyone away.
now: The masjid committee wants the big donor at the front and the quiet uncle who sweeps the floor out of sight. The work group chat has an inner circle. {idea}Nuh kept the poor believers at his side{/idea} even when it cost him the powerful.
old: To get the influential people on board, I may have to sideline the ordinary ones.
new: Those who turned to Allah keep their place, whatever it costs me with the powerful.
try: Sit with or message someone at your masjid or work whom others usually overlook.

title: Who would protect me if I pushed them out?
subtitle: Rejecting the humble has its own reckoning

row.title: Allah's displeasure
sub: no one shields me from it

then: Nuh kept answering the chiefs who wanted the weak believers gone. He turned their demand around: {trap}if I drove them away, who would help me against Allah?{/trap} Then he asked them to {idea}stop and think{/idea}.
now: You are planning the wedding guest list and someone says to cut the relatives who "do not fit." Or a manager asks you to quietly freeze out the new hire nobody likes. {idea}Ask Nuh's question.{/idea} Whose displeasure are you really avoiding?
old: Losing the approval of important people is the bigger risk.
new: Wronging a humble believer puts me against Allah, and no one can shield me from that.
try: Before you leave someone out of something this week, ask yourself who you are pleasing by it.

title: No treasures, no unseen, no angel, no judging hearts.
subtitle: Nuh says honestly what he is not

key.label: The people you look down on

then: Nuh told his people plainly that he was {idea}only a human messenger{/idea}. He did not hold Allah's treasures, know the unseen, or claim to be an angel. And he would not say of the believers they looked down on that {trap}Allah would give them no good{/trap}. Allah knows what is inside them.
now: At the bus stop you see a man in a stained jacket, mumbling, and something in you files him as worthless. In the office you quietly rank people by title. {idea}You do not see souls.{/idea} The one your eyes dismiss may be dearer to Allah than you.
old: I can tell what a person is worth from how they look and where they stand.
new: Only Allah knows what is inside a soul, so writing someone off would make me the wrongdoer.
try: Catch one quick judgment you make about a stranger today and replace it with a silent prayer for them.

title: Enough talking, bring the punishment then.
subtitle: Tired of argument, they dare the warning
then: After long years of Nuh's advice, his people gave their final word. {trap}You have argued with us long enough, and we still will not follow you.{/trap} They asked him to bring the punishment he warned of, hurrying Allah's anger on themselves rather than change.
now: Your doctor has warned you about your blood sugar three visits in a row. You roll your eyes and say "we all die of something." {idea}A dare can be a way of not listening.{/idea} Sometimes "bring it on" just means "I will not change."
old: Challenging a warning shows I am not afraid of it.
new: Daring the warning to come is often just a way to avoid changing.
try: Think of one warning you keep brushing off, about health, money, or faith. Write down one small step you could take.

title: The punishment is not mine to bring.
subtitle: Nuh points them away from himself to Allah
then: They had dared Nuh to bring the punishment. He did not boast or threaten back. {idea}Only Allah brings it, if He wills{/idea}, he said, and {trap}no one can escape Him{/trap}. The warner is only a messenger, not the one in control.
now: Someone mocks you: "So where is this Day you keep talking about?" You feel you need to prove it on the spot. {idea}You do not hold the timing.{/idea} You can only say what you know and leave the rest with Allah.
old: If I cannot prove the warning right now, I look foolish.
new: The outcome and its timing belong to Allah; I am only asked to speak honestly.
try: When someone challenges your faith today, answer briefly and calmly, without needing to win.

title: Good advice cannot help a heart that refuses it.
subtitle: Sincere counsel has limits, and all return to Him
then: Nuh admitted the limit of his own effort. {trap}My advice will not benefit you{/trap} if Allah's will is to leave you astray. Then he reminded them who they were dealing with: {idea}He is your Lord, and to Him you will return{/idea}, the One who owns how every matter ends.
now: You have sent your friend article after article about leaving a harmful habit. You rewrite the perfect message at 1 a.m. {idea}Advice is your part. Guidance is Allah's.{/idea} You can give your best and still not be the one who changes a heart.
old: If they do not change, I must not have said it well enough.
new: I give sincere advice; whether it benefits is in Allah's hands, and we all return to Him.
try: Make dua tonight for one person you have been trying to advise, instead of sending another message.

title: If I made it up, the sin is mine alone.
subtitle: A pause in Nuh's story to answer Makkah
then: In the middle of Nuh's story, Allah turns to the Prophet ﷺ. The disbelievers of Makkah said {trap}he made this up{/trap}. He is told to answer: if I invented it, the crime is mine alone. {idea}But I am innocent of what you do.{/idea} The one who knows Allah's punishment for lying about Him would not lie.
now: Someone in the comments says your faith is something you were just taught and never checked. You feel defensive. {idea}You answer for your own choices{/idea}, and so do they. That thought is calming, not cold.
old: I have to defend myself against every accusation or it will stick.
new: Each person carries their own deeds before Allah; I only need to be honest in mine.
try: Let one unfair comment about you go unanswered today, and check only that your own conduct is clean.

title: No one else will believe. Do not grieve.
subtitle: Allah lifts the weight off Nuh's shoulders

row.title: their choices
sub: as if they were his fault

then: Nuh's people had hurried Allah's punishment on themselves, and Nuh had called to his Lord that he was overcome. Then came the revelation: {idea}none of your people will believe except those who already have{/idea}. {reward}So do not be distressed by what they do.{/reward}
now: You have kept the family together for years: the calls, the peace-making, the hosting. Some relatives still turn away. {reward}You are allowed to stop carrying their choices.{/reward} Doing your part is not the same as owning their response.
old: If they do not respond, it is a failure I must keep grieving.
new: Once I have done my part, Allah Himself tells me not to be crushed by others' choices.
try: Name one person whose choices you keep blaming yourself for. Say: I did my part, the rest is with Allah.

title: Build the ship under Our eyes.
subtitle: Work done while Allah watches and teaches
then: Allah told Nuh to build the ship {reward}under Our eyes and with Our revelation{/reward}, meaning He would watch and teach him what to do. Nuh was also told not to plead for the wrongdoers anymore. {trap}Their drowning had been decided.{/trap}
now: You are on a long night shift, or patching code nobody will praise, or cooking for a family that barely says thanks. It feels unseen. {idea}It is under His eyes.{/idea} Nuh's planks were not glamorous either.
old: Work nobody notices does not really count.
new: Every plank I lay is seen by Allah, and He guides the work I do for Him.
try: Before one ordinary task today, say quietly: You see this, so help me do it well.

title: They laughed at a ship on dry land.
subtitle: Mockery while obeying, and Nuh's steady reply
then: Nuh kept building. {trap}Every time the chiefs of his people passed, they mocked him{/trap}, rejecting his warning that they would drown. He did not stop. He answered that if they laughed now, {idea}the laughter would one day turn back on them{/idea}.
now: Your coworkers smirk when you step out to pray. Your friends tease you for skipping the bar night or saving instead of spending. {idea}Keep building.{/idea} Mockery is loud today, but it does not decide how things end.
old: If people laugh at what I am doing, maybe I am the one who is wrong.
new: Mockery does not make obedience foolish; the end will show who was right.
try: The next time someone teases you for a good habit, smile, say nothing back, and carry on.

title: Soon you will know who is disgraced.
subtitle: Two outcomes, here and after

row.title: the final outcome
sub: who is honored, who is not

then: Nuh finished his answer to the mockers with {trap}a serious warning{/trap}. They would soon see who would be humiliated in this life and who would face a lasting punishment after it. {idea}The scene at the shipyard was not the end of the story.{/idea}
now: You scroll past a clip of someone being mocked for their faith, and you laugh along before you think. Or you are the one laughed at. {idea}Today's laughter is not the last word.{/idea} Ask which side of that warning your own habits are building toward.
old: What people think of me right now is what matters.
new: The real outcome comes later, and it is my conduct, not the crowd, that decides it.
try: Skip or report one video today that mocks someone's faith instead of sharing it.
